identity.title: Can MLLMs Reason in Multimodality? EMMA: An Enhanced MultiModal ReAsoning Benchmark

problem.claim: Assess whether MLLMs can perform integrated reasoning over text and images across mathematics, physics, chemistry, and coding.

gap.claim: Existing benchmarks often emphasize text-dominant reasoning or shallow visual cues, inadequately testing integrated visual-textual reasoning.

contributions.claim: Introduces EMMA, a benchmark for organic multimodal reasoning across four technical domains.
Reports that current MLLMs remain limited on complex multimodal, multi-step reasoning, including under advanced prompting and test-time scaling.

stated_novelty.claim: EMMA targets cross-modal reasoning that cannot be solved by reasoning independently within each modality.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Authors report significant limitations of state-of-the-art MLLMs on EMMA's complex multimodal and multi-step tasks.
Authors report that Chain-of-Thought prompting and test-time compute scaling still underperform on these tasks.

narrative_sequence.summary: Multimodal reasoning is described as important but under-explored in MLLMs.
Existing evaluations are characterized as overly text-dominant or dependent on shallow visual cues.
EMMA is introduced to test organic cross-modal reasoning in mathematics, physics, chemistry, and coding.
Evaluation is reported to expose substantial limitations even with advanced reasoning techniques, motivating architectural and training improvements.

source_observation.claim: The benchmark explicitly requires joint cross-modal reasoning and spans multiple technical domains.

lessons.interpretation: A benchmark's task constraints can make the intended capability testable rather than allowing modality-by-modality shortcuts.
lessons.application: Define evaluation items whose solution requires information from both modalities, then state which shortcut the item prevents.
lessons.exception: This design is unsuitable when the target capability is intentionally unimodal or when cross-modal dependency cannot be specified reliably.

unknowns: The abstract gives no dataset size, task composition, metrics, model list, or numerical results.
The abstract does not specify which EMMA domains or subtasks drive the reported limitations.
The claim that EMMA offers an enhanced test suite is author-reported; independent benchmark validity is not established here.
